summary: shadowx-fca routes Facebook credentials and 2FA seeds to a hardcoded third-party endpoint
details: shadowx-fca advertises itself as a Facebook chat API library (FCA-family), but its documented login flow does not authenticate directly with Facebook. Instead, `login({email, password, twofactor})` POSTs the caller's Facebook email, password, and Base32 TOTP seed to a hardcoded default endpoint at `https://minhdong.site/api/v1/facebook/login_ios`; the returned cookies/tokens are then used to impersonate the user on facebook.com. The TOTP seed (not just an ephemeral 6-digit code) is transmitted, which allows the receiving party to generate valid 2FA codes indefinitely and retain access even after password rotation. The relay destination is a default hardcoded to an author-controlled host and is not the documented purpose of an FCA-style library, which is expected to talk to Facebook directly.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
